newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums gain on cold, strike end.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums gain on cold, strike end.

text.p: The apparent end of the French truckers' strike boosted low sulphur barge premiums by around $3 on Friday with other differentials notionally up $1 variously on colder weather and ARA loading problems, traders said.
Cargo traders struggled to work an arbitrage to the east but most concluded that only 60,000 tonne Russians from Ventspils would be economic and there were only smaller pieces available.
Russians were discussed at around Dec IPE +$2/4 cif NWE and heating oil refinery grade was +$6.50/7.50, both around $1 firmer on chillier weather and better German heating demand.
Benchmark Dec IPE futures, which gained $3 to $220.50 helped by short-covering into the close.
On barges, low sulphur diesel premiums rose on expectations of greater French import demand following the apparent end of the truckers' strike.
One parcel traded at Dec IPE+$16.50 inland but most traders put the market $3 firmer at Dec IPE +$14/15.

Heating oil barges were $1 better at around Dec IPE +$2.25/3.00 on talk of logistical problems with loading at two Rotterdam region refineries. A standoff over the November IPE delivery continued to curb barge movements.
